title: chore: Remove websockets<16.0 pin once py-shinywidgets issue is resolved
description:
## Remove websockets<16.0 pin once py-shinywidgets issue is resolved

**Background:**
We've pinned `websockets<16.0` in 5 template requirements.txt files to work around a breaking change in websockets 16.0 that causes anywidget initialization failures.

**Affected Templates:**
- `nba-dashboard/requirements.txt`
- `dashboard-tips/requirements.txt`
- `stock-app/requirements.txt`
- `monitor-database/requirements.txt`
- `map-distance/requirements.txt`

**Upstream Issue:**
This is tracked in py-shinywidgets: https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shinywidgets/issues/218

**Root Cause:**
websockets commit [`69ec85e`](https://github.com/python-websockets/websockets/commit/69ec85e67ace98ba334010d1e893cfb67de5f2e9) (released in websockets 16.0 on Jan 10, 2026) breaks anywidget model initialization, causing this browser error:
```
Uncaught (in promise) Error: [anywidget] Failed to initialize model.
```

**TODO:**
Once the py-shinywidgets issue is resolved (either via a fix in py-shinywidgets or websockets), remove the `websockets<16.0` pin from all affected requirements.txt files.

**How to Check if Fixed:**
1. Install latest versions of all packages (no pins)
2. Run each affected template
3. Verify no "[anywidget] Failed to initialize model" errors in browser console
4. If all templates work, remove the websockets pin

**Current Pin Location:**
All files have this comment block:
```
# websockets 16.0+ breaks anywidget initialization
# See https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shinywidgets/issues/218
websockets<16.0
```

title: Add example with plot theming with dark mode or shinyswatch
Syntax for installing from GitHub
description:
The syntax for installing from GitHub is a little too low-level

```bash
shiny create -m core -g https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny-templates/tree/main/basic-navigation
```

It'd be nice if we could break this into smaller pieces

```
shiny create -m core --github posit-dev/py-shiny-templates basic-navigation
```

or abstractly

```
shiny create -m core [--github <repo> --ref <ref>] path/to/template
```

We could also consider replacing `--github` with `--repo` and assuming `--repo` is GitHub, but it could in the future be any git-backed repo.

title: nba-dashboard: `ff.create_distplot` was removed in plotly 7.0.0
description:
`nba-dashboard` fails at runtime with:

```
File "nba-dashboard/plots.py", line 41, in density_plot
    fig = ff.create_distplot(
AttributeError: module 'plotly.figure_factory' has no attribute 'create_distplot'
```

## Cause

[plotly 7.0.0](https://github.com/plotly/plotly.py/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) (released 2026-08-25) removed twelve deprecated Figure Factory functions ([plotly/plotly.py#5627](https://github.com/plotly/plotly.py/pull/5627)), `create_distplot` among them:

> Remove the deprecated Figure Factory functions `create_2d_density`, `create_annotated_heatmap`, `create_bullet`, `create_candlestick`, `create_choropleth`, `create_distplot`, `create_facet_grid`, `create_gantt`, `create_hexbin_mapbox`, `create_ohlc`, `create_scatterplotmatrix`, and `create_violin`

`nba-dashboard/requirements.txt` pins `plotly` unpinned, so fresh installs now get 7.0.0.

`create_distplot` is the only removed function used anywhere in this repo — I grepped all twelve across every `.py` here, and `plots.py:41` is the single hit. So this one call site is the whole fix.

## Scope

`density_plot()` in `nba-dashboard/plots.py` uses the returned figure's internals afterwards, so a replacement has to preserve that shape:

- `fig.data[0]` is the KDE curve — `hoverinfo`, `showlegend`, and `.y.max()` (used to size the players' vertical lines) are all read off it
- `fig.data[1]` is the rug — `hoverinfo`, and `customdata` is set to `person_id` to drive the `on_rug_click` handler

So it needs a KDE trace plus a rug trace, in that order. Options: compute the KDE directly (`scipy.stats.gaussian_kde`, already an indirect dependency) and add a `Scatter` plus a rug `Scatter`, or vendor the small part of the old `create_distplot` that this uses.

## Impact beyond this repo

This also fails py-shiny's CI: its `playwright-examples` job checks out this repo's default branch unpinned and runs every template, so the breakage lands on unrelated py-shiny PRs. Tracked at posit-dev/py-shiny#2476.

Example failing run (from py-shiny#2475, whose changes are unrelated): https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/actions/runs/33005424806/job/98297807809
